opening.argument: The video explains what a CP 2000 notice means, how the IRS calculates proposed additional taxes, and why taxpayers must respond within 60 days. It also discusses common response errors, placing the recommendation to work with the speaker's team and CryptoTaxAudit within practical tax guidance. The description expressly frames the material as educational and informational. Although the speaker reports that the team has had a 40% refund rate by identifying mistakes in taxpayers' initial returns, that is presented as a past outcome, not a guaranteed refund or a requirement that viewers participate financially.

citations.quote: CP 2000 letter is a letter sent to a taxpayer saying, Hey, we think you forgot to report some income, and generally cites 1099 form of some type.
they calculate what they think the additional taxes are on the unreported income, and they're going to expect payment within a short period of time unless you write back to them within 60 days
we've had over a 40% refund rate, where, actually, we showed the IRS that mistakes had been made even by the taxpayers initial return, and we get refunds back.
This video is for educational and informational purposes only and does not constitute legal, tax, or financial advice.
